title: Listed Table Format

illustrates.quote: Wide Tables: Listed Table Format. The listed table format repeats the column heading for each entry. This is useful for tables with numerous columns, columns of numbers, repetitive entries, or nonintuitive entries. (See Sample 11-24: Listed Table Format on page 11-50.)

print.notes: Each cell that holds more than one office-holder shows them on separate lines in print (and, matching that, on separate indented braille lines -- see braille.lines 12-14 for Sec of State, 15-16 for Sec of Treasury); multiple names are joined here with '\n' to preserve that one-per-line structure rather than inventing a print punctuation mark that is not actually there. Secretary of Navy did not exist until 1798 and is genuinely blank for the Washington administration. See 'Unresolved' in the README for the Secretary-of-War/Secretary-of-Navy braille anomaly.
print.printFeatures: Small-caps bold section label (PRESIDENTIAL ADMINISTRATIONS) above a bordered box, alternating light-grey/white row shading, ruled column dividers, bold column headers.

braille.notes: The eight print columns become the Listed Table Format: a transcriber's note (lines 4-10) explains the change (print format is changed; row headings are blocked in cell 2; column headings are repeated for clarity; a colon separates headings from table entries; plus the guide-dots-blank-entry sample sentence). The body then lists Washington's administration as a cell-5 heading (President: George Washington 1789-1797, lines 12-13), followed by each subsequent column heading plus colon plus value: Vice President (single entry, lines 14-15), Sec of State (three entries, heading line 16 + indented entries lines 17-19), Sec of Treasury (two entries, heading line 20 + indented entries lines 21-22), Sec of War (heading line 23), then a line reading only '444' (line 24), then Sec of Navy (heading line 25) followed inline by three double-quote guide-dot characters.

uncertain: See the section README's 'Known uncertainties and source errata' list: Secretary of War's braille entry (line 24) is just the token '444' where print shows three named office-holders; flagged for Paul.
resolution: print.rows: multiple office-holders within one cell are joined with a newline to preserve print's (and braille's) one-name-per-line layout, rather than inventing a print punctuation mark ('/' in run A, ';' in run B) that is not actually there (confirmed against both the PDF image, pp. 332-333, and the source .txt's own indented one-name-per-braille-line layout for Sec of State/Treasury). See 'Unresolved' in the README for the Secretary-of-War/-Navy braille anomaly that both runs flagged.
